name: Syntactic DNA Watermarking
description: Detects the presence of cryptographic or statistical 'watermarks' invisibly embedded into the text during the AI generation process. Many modern Large Language Models employ techniques like 'Green-Red List Partitioning' (Kirchenbauer et al., 2023) to intentionally inject a mathematically detectable signature into their output. During generation, the model's vocabulary is pseudo-randomly divided into 'green' (promoted) and 'red' (penalized) tokens based on the hash of the preceding word. By analyzing the token sequence and reverse-engineering this statistical bias, the algorithm can definitively prove AI authorship, as human writers naturally select words without these hidden probabilistic constraints.
mechanism: The algorithm processes the text token by token, attempting to reconstruct the pseudo-random hashing function that may have been used by an AI to partition its vocabulary. It calculates the statistical frequency of consecutive 'green' tokens over a specific window. A standard, unwatermarked human text will naturally exhibit a roughly 50/50 distribution of pseudo-randomly hashed 'green' and 'red' tokens. A mathematically significant overrepresentation of 'green' tokens constitutes an undeniable cryptographic fingerprint of machine generation.
useCase: The ultimate definitive test for detecting text generated by commercial LLMs that comply with AI safety transparency standards and embed invisible watermarks.
strengths:
• Approaching 100% certainty (near-zero false positive rate) if the specific watermark hashing algorithm of the source AI model is known.
• Highly robust against light human editing, synonym substitution, or adversarial paraphrasing, as the statistical 'DNA' persists across the broader document.
limitations:
• Completely ineffective if the AI model used for generation is open-source, heavily quantized, or simply does not employ an active watermarking protocol.
• Requires a sufficiently long text snippet (typically 50+ tokens) to prove statistical significance and trigger the mathematical threshold.
parameters:
Analysis: Cryptographic Token-Hash Verification
Metric: Green-List Token Bias & Distribution Variance
Output: 0-100 Mathematical Watermark Certainty Score
accuracy: Definitive — >99% standalone accuracy if a known watermark is present. Fails gracefully (no false positives) if the text is unwatermarked.
